deploy-bot: [AUTO] Release 2.9.0-canary-3 blocked in us-west-2. Reason: SBOM provenance mismatch for component 'github.com/libfastkv' (detected artifact vs declared). Transitive vuln detected: CVE-2026-1234 (CVSS 8.2). Quarantining canary. Pipeline: /pipelines/1234 :rotating_light:

Olivia (release): Ack. Which pipelines/regions are affected?

Nate: Only canary in us-west-2 right now. Other regions didn't complete canary rollout yet.

Security Team: We see libfastkv@v1.2.3 present in SBOM but provenance signature doesn't match the known builder key. Upstream has a patch at v1.2.4 that claims fix for CVE-2026-1234, but we don't have a signed provenance artifact for 1.2.4 on our mirror.

Dave (SRE): Impact? Is this a runtime exploit path for our prod traffic, or just a library-level advisory?

Security Team: It's exploitable in certain edge cases (deserialization flow used by our ingestion). Canary observed no active exploit, but severity + provenance mismatch -> policy says block auto-promotion. :eyes:

Carol (Product): We intended to ship release notes and changelog today. If we delay, we need a short comms plan for customers.

Olivia (release): Options I see: 1) Pin transitive dep to a previously verified version (e.g., v1.2.2) and cut a hotfix branch, 2) Wait for upstream signed provenance for 1.2.4 and then consume, 3) Rollback canary and abort global release until verification. Change window opens at 22:00 PST — need a decision before then.

Nate: I can open a patch branch now. Quick pin in go.mod would be:```
replace github.com/libfastkv v1.2.3 => v1.2.2
// then `go mod tidy` and rebuild images```
I'll also run a local SBOM generation to check runtime image provenance.

Security Team: We want either pinned + verified provenance, or evidence of secure rebuild by our CI (signed SLSA attestation). If you go pinned-to-1.2.2, we need a vuln scan after rebuild.

Dave (SRE): If we decide rollback, rollback command is: `./scripts/rollback-release --release 2.9.0 --region us-west-2` — that will revert canary instances and unblock other pipelines. I can run it in 10m if we approve.

Legal: If the release goes out with a known exploitable CVE (even transitive) we need to pre-clear the messaging. If the fix is not provenance-verified, we need to mark it in release notes and escalate to enterprise accounts.

Olivia (release): Proposed decision: Pause global rollout, rollback the quarantined canary in us-west-2, create INF-4520 to track hotfix + SBOM provenance verification, and delay publication of release notes until we have either pinned rebuild or signed upstream artifact. Anyone object? :thinking_face:

Nate: No objection. I'll open the hotfix branch 2.9.1-hotfix and push the replace / rebuild.

Security Team: Please attach the new SBOM + SLSA attestation to INF-4520. We'll run a targeted vuln scan and then sign-off.

Dave (SRE): Rolling back now. Running: `./scripts/rollback-release --release 2.9.0 --region us-west-2 --force`

deploy-bot: [AUTO] Rollback started for 2.9.0 in us-west-2. Status: in-progress. Linked issue INF-4520 created.

Carol (Product): I'll hold the release notes — will prepare an explanatory blurb we can reuse once the team confirms remediation.

Legal: I'll draft a short customer note template in case enterprise customers ask before we re-release.

Olivia (release): Thanks all. Nate — once you have a rebuilt image with pinned dep and SBOM + attestation, post here and Security will do a final scan. Everyone else, stand by for INF-4520 updates. :thumbsup:
